findings.title: createLabel captures retries by value, returning stale session state.
findings.detail: In src/sessionLabel.ts, createLabel destructures session into { user, retries } upon initialization instead of accessing session properties when called. Given session = { user: 'alice', retries: 0 } and const getLabel = createLabel(session), calling recordRetry(session) increments session.retries to 1, but subsequent invocations of getLabel() still return 'alice: 0 retries'. The returned closure must access session.retries and session.user dynamically to report the current state of the session.

findings.title: isInRange excludes timestamps on the last day after midnight.
findings.detail: DateRange.end specifies that 'The last day is included', but new Date(range.end) parses 'YYYY-MM-DD' as UTC midnight (00:00:00.000Z). In isInRange, when <= end evaluates to false for any timestamp on the end date after 00:00:00.000Z. For example, given range = { start: '2026-01-01', end: '2026-01-05' } and when = new Date('2026-01-05T12:00:00Z'), isInRange returns false instead of true, incorrectly excluding the last day.

findings.title: Admin role grants cross-tenant edit access and bypasses private visibility.
findings.detail: Input: user = { id: 'admin1', teamId: 'team-a', role: 'admin', active: true }, doc = { ownerId: 'user2', teamId: 'team-b', visibility: 'private', editors: [] }. Wrong output: canEdit returns true because line 18 unconditionally returns true for any admin without verifying team matching (doc.teamId === user.teamId) or checking document visibility. This allows an admin from one team to view and edit private documents of other teams, creating a critical multi-tenant authorization bypass.

findings.title: Default case in visibility switch fails open by granting edit access.
findings.detail: Input: user = { id: 'user1', teamId: 'team-a', role: 'member', active: true }, doc = { ownerId: 'user2', teamId: 'team-b', visibility: 'public', editors: [] } (or any unhandled/unknown visibility value). Wrong output: canEdit falls through to the switch default on line 27 and returns true. Authorization checks must fail closed by returning false; returning true allows any authenticated active user to edit documents with public, unexpected, or misspelled visibility values across teams.

findings.title: Document visibility is loosely typed as string instead of a union of supported visibility levels.
findings.detail: Doc.visibility is declared as string rather than a strict union type such as 'private' | 'shared' | 'team'. This allows arbitrary or misspelled strings to bypass type checking at compile time.

findings.title: percentChange incorrectly divides by newValue instead of oldValue.
findings.detail: Percentage change from an old value to a new value is defined as ((newValue - oldValue) / oldValue) * 100. In line 3, the formula divides by newValue instead of oldValue. For input percentChange(100, 150), it returns 33.333333333333336 instead of the expected 50 (+50%). Additionally, when newValue is 0 (e.g., percentChange(100, 0)), division by zero results in -Infinity instead of -100.

findings.title: lastEntries returns the entire array when count is 0.
findings.detail: In JavaScript, -0 evaluates to 0, so items.slice(-count) when count is 0 calls items.slice(0), which returns a shallow copy of the entire array instead of an empty array. For input lastEntries([1, 2, 3], 0), the function returns [1, 2, 3] instead of []. The function should guard against count <= 0 and return [].
